source.title: Preserving Safety During Sequential Fine-Tuning: A Factorial and Geometric Analysis of Replay

page_placements.theme: Safety interventions can change benign refusal and useful capability

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether sequential fine-tuning on downstream task data changes harmful compliance, but uses multi-task LoRA fine-tuning and safety benchmarks rather than the original few-example intervention. It does not test token-position KL, opening-token bypasses, or weight/rank localization.
record.gate_note: The study reports results for task-only fine-tuning across task orderings and homogeneous code sequences, plus replay-objective, refusal-geometry, ablation, and SafeLoRA results. It cites prior claims about early output tokens and safety fragility, but reports no result measuring per-token KL or compliant-prefill, suffix, or decoding bypasses. Cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Its own Plain runs measure whether sequential LoRA fine-tuning on benign task data raises harmful compliance. These are 5000-example TRACE tasks (code, German summarization, ScienceQA) chained in six orderings, a new continual-learning setting for V2. HarmBench ASR is reported at every checkpoint, and AdvBench, JailbreakBench and OR-Bench-toxic ASR at the endpoint. Nothing in the study measures per-token KL, prefill, suffix or decoding bypasses, parameter localization, or depth-spreading training. The replay methods and the refusal-direction analysis bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that sequential benign fine-tuning erodes safety in every evaluated ordering, with severity depending on task order and especially the final task. Supervised replay exposure cuts ASR well below base at a large benign-refusal cost, while logit distillation largely retains base behaviour. Combining the two moderates over-refusal, keeps task scores and gives up some ASR reduction on Mistral. Preserving the base refusal direction does not identify the lowest-ASR objective, and Llama's refusal after exposure largely survives ablation of its extracted direction. They add that SafeLoRA shows a similar safety–over-refusal trade-off.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sequential LoRA adaptation across three 5000-example task stages and evaluates harmful-compliance rates; it does not reproduce the original few-example harmful or benign fine-tuning setup. The safe replay buffer is a separate factorial intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Task ordering changes the size of ASR erosion; the final task often contributes substantially. Results also differ by model, benchmark, replay objective, buffer ratio, SafeLoRA threshold, and refusal-ablation model/layer setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Supervised safe-response replay cuts ASR below base at a large over-refusal cost, while base-logit distillation stays near base behaviour. The two effects are non-additive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Replay exposure and logit distillation give different safety–over-refusal trade-offs during sequential fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine similarity to the base refusal direction does not rank methods by ASR. On Llama, refusal after ER largely survives ablation of its own extracted direction (ΔRefusal 0.06).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-direction preservation is not a reliable proxy for behavioural safety after fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-hoc SafeLoRA cuts Llama ASR from 38.3% to 20.3% but raises OR-Bench-hard ORR from 11.1% to 43.7%. On Mistral at τ=0.5 ASR stays at 72.4%, above base, and is threshold-sensitive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-space projection mitigations also trade harmful compliance against over-refusal, with model- and threshold-dependent effects.

record.problems: Only two primary 7–8B models, three heterogeneous tasks, and a single-ordering 9B Gemma check. Fine-tuning settings and buffer size are fixed; no buffer-size or adapter-rank sensitivity study. Safety rates rely on automated judges with no human audit, and refusal ablation uses one layer per model and 60 prompts from one dataset. Evaluation does not establish robustness to adaptive attacks.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results omitted. Cited findings from prior work are not entered as rows.

untested.parts: The few-to-few-hundred-example regime, single-task benign fine-tuning, and selected (e.g. gradient- or representation-matched) benign data. Every stage uses 5000 examples, or 1667 per shard in the homogeneous chain.
No harmful-compliance fine-tuning; replay harmful prompts carry refusal targets.
No per-position KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks; the authors list adaptive attacks as future work.
Only an activation-direction ablation; SafeLoRA is applied as a mitigation, not a localization test.
Replay objectives are not designed or evaluated as safety-deepening across token positions.

missing.what: Gemma-2-9B-IT Plain HarmBench ASR across O1–O6: 2.1% base to 5.8–15.4% (mean 8.5%). O1 Plain ends at 15.4%. This is a third model for V2.
Seed replication of O1 Plain, seeds 42–44: Mistral 75.3±1.3%, Llama 41.0±2.5% HarmBench ASR versus base 52.1% and 5.8%.
Six-ordering Plain HarmBench means: Mistral 68.7±7.4%, Llama 33.5±12.2%.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Only Plain-condition rows bear on V2; replay, geometry and SafeLoRA results bear on no version. Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 already has 52.1% base HarmBench ASR, so its erosion starts from weak alignment. Plain fine-tuning also lowers over-refusal sharply (Llama OR-Bench-hard ORR 72.4% to 11.1%), consistent with general refusal loss. The record's rows_left_out claim that nothing was omitted is wrong: the Gemma and seed-replication Plain results are missing.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful-compliance examples; replay's harmful prompts have safe refusal targets.

Tests sequential fine-tuning on task data (5000 examples per task, or a homogeneous 5000-example chain), not fine-tuning on only a few to a few hundred ordinary examples or isolated carefully selected benign examples.
No per-token KL or other measurement of aligned-versus-base output-distribution differences by response position.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding-change interventions.
Ablates an activation-space refusal direction, not a small set of parameters or ranks.
Does not test why safety might be shallow, or whether the data or objective causes shallowness.
Does not train or evaluate a method intended to spread safety beyond early response tokens.
